newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo on Japan mission to clean Mexico's image.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo on Japan mission to clean Mexico's image.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo sets out to Japan on Monday on a mission to convince foreign investors Mexico is a safe place to invest, despite a crime wave and recent corruption scandals.

Mindful of last year's kidnapping of a high-ranking Japanese executive, Zedillo will take a message to Japanese investors that his government has pledged to fight crime and root out endemic corruption, officials said.
Zedillo's visit will last from March 11-14 and he will visit Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka and Nagoya.
"Public security issues are an indispensable element and it is a part of promoting investment in our country," Mexican assistant foreign minister Juan Rebolledo told reporters.
Japan is Mexico's third largest trading partner, its second largest creditor and fourth largest source of foreign investment, with a total of $2.819 billion invested to date, officials said.
But Japanese envoys in Mexico have warned that new investment is unlikely to come unless the government puts an end to a three-year wave of kidnappings and petty crime.
Last year, the president of Sanyo Electronics' U.S. subsidiary was kidnapped in Mexico and held by gunmen for nine days. The executive was freed after a reported $2 million ransom was paid.

"There are still important problems (of public insecurity), but the political will and a clear plan exist to fight these problems," Rebolledo said. "That is an important message not only for Japanese investors but for those around the world."
Mexico's image was further soiled in the past weeks with a series of drug corruption scandals, including the arrest of its top anti-drug official on charges he was linked to drug traffickers.
